nodes.text:
#Glad you're here.

You've entered the Public Intercept, my experiment in building a new kind of website and publishing platform. 

As of August 2026, I've started adding content, but the offerings are still pretty sparse. I'm trying to remedy that as quickly as possible, but there are already a few things here worth checking out. 

I've included some information on how to use the site, but most of you will probably figure it out by poking around. 

Obviously this platform is multimedia and one of the best ways to use it on mobile is to install it as a web app. There's a link to the simple instructions on how to do that just below the button you clicked to read this. 

Lots of updates coming, glad to have you along!

-Matt

nodes.title: In Stride - Demo
nodes.text:
# In Stride

Halfway there I found myself
Before I began
Searching for a message 
That I held in my hand
I recognized the words
But I could not understand
'Til I read it in a different light

Once I had arrived 
I couldn't find my way there
Lost contact with the ground
My legs were swinging in the air
It felt a little strange
When blind men started to stare
But they saw it in a different light

### Chorus:
Every day and night
I'm taking it all in stride
I'm taking it all in stride
And I'm busting apart at the seams baby
Nothing's at all what it seems, maybe
Reality feels like a dream
When I open my eyes
But I'm taking it all in stride

### Chorus

Now I'm going nowhere
'Cause I've been there before
Found a ladder to the matter
Laying on the floor
My mind was just an anchor 
'Til it started to soar
Now I'm thinking in a different light

Every day and night...

### Chorus

©Matthew Sigmon

Recorded Jan 14, 1999

## Feel It - Song Sketch
_Recorded Jan 14, 1999_


You can push on love
'Cause love will push on you
Make your plans and take your stands
Does it take you where you want it to?
When the words are nowhere found
You and silence find common ground

**Chorus:**
And you feel it
You've got to feel it
If you want to live
Oh can you feel it?
Feel it and give
What you have to give

Sometimes it hurts you
Sometimes it heals
Sometimes it brings riches untold
And sometimes it steals
Sometimes you've got to throw away
The rules you'd rather 
Make the wind obey

**Chorus**

links.text: Supernormal Radio website

nodes.text:
#Streaming radio that sounds like radio.

I made my planet Earth debut at the ass end of 1963, making me a closing bell Boomer, and a 3rd quarter member of Generation Jones. In other words, I'm officially physiologically mature. 

When I run into people who were born in the 1990s and beyond, I feel compelled to let them know they missed a ton of great stuff by showing up late. They missed a world where time and space were experienced viscerally, consciously, directly. It could be amazingly quiet in the 1970s, until you turned the radio on, which I did just about every chance I got. 

I grew up in west central Illinois, at the time, a region of serious media austerity. 2 TV channels (NBC and CBS, which meant we couldn't watch "Happy Days"), and only a few more radio stations than that. Chicago's 890 WLS and 55 KSD in St. Louis were the big AM blowtorches, and that's where I discovered music on the radio.

There was an FM station, KGRC in Hannibal/Quincy, and my oldest sister had a nice little Sony portable radio that was usually tuned to it.  But I liked WLS, I liked AM radio and how music sounded on it.  I still do. 

Unlike the streaming platforms today, AM radio had its own personality and moods—they changed with the weather. On a rainy day, the signal might be so buried in static that you'd only get parts and pieces of what the DJ was spinning. But when you did, it landed like a cool glass of water on a hot summer day, it quenched something, connected you to a world of sound, expression, melody, and meaning.

AM radio made music available, and also scarce. Tuning in a station when reception was dicey felt like a negotiation, equal parts skill and luck. If conditions were just right, you became an eavesdropper, tugging a tenuous thread of culture, art, and excitement out of the ethers. You felt lucky, and you were. 

The essence of those experiences are powerfully linked to the unique sonic qualities of the medium, and that's why I created Supernormal Radio. 

This stream rotates over 2000 tracks from the 50s through the 90s (and a few from later), each one treated and re-recorded to faithfully capture the sound of a vintage AM broadcast. You can listen to this on your phone and you'll have a pretty good idea what it was like to carry around a transistor radio the size of a deck of cards. 

There's more to music than high fidelity and recording quality. Check out the stream and who knows, maybe you'll see what I mean.
